<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1210
Claimant:
Jeremy Hicks
Adjuster:
Chelsea Hebert
09/07/2023
Claim received by phone from the policyholder's driver reporting a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection
earlier today, with a report of a wrist injury to the claimant.
10/01/2023
Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file
suggests the damage happened before coverage began.
10/31/2023
Claimant is not represented by an attorney. Statement taken and recorded; the claimant described stopping behind a
vehicle that did not move in time to avoid contact.
12/08/2023
Reviewed photos submitted by the claimant. They confirm the rear bumper and tail lamp damage on the claimant's
vehicle and the front-end damage on the other vehicle, which line up well with the described impact.
02/22/2024
Medical records show a wrist fracture consistent in kind and force with the crash as described. No prior injury to the
same body area is known from the claimant's history or available records.
04/06/2024
Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this type of fracture. Follow-up notes are being
requested to confirm the reason for the extended course.
04/07/2024
Claimant was contacted for a follow-up call. Added a few small details about the sequence of events, but the core
account has stayed the same since the first report.
04/15/2024
No independent witnesses have been identified. The only available accounts are the claimant's and the other driver's,
plus the photos on file.
04/23/2024
Some uncertainty remains about where the claimant was seated in the vehicle at impact. The claimant has not been
able to clarify this in a way that resolves the question, so it will be noted in the file.
04/25/2024
Vehicle damage has been reviewed against the described impact and matches it. No earlier damage to the vehicle is
known from prior claims or inspection records.
04/26/2024
File is being referred for the next review step. Open items are the extended treatment records and the seating
position question, and the claim remains under standard handling.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
